claims.text: The initial Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy is a single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy.
Asymmetric XRD peaks in the initial alloy result from compositional micro-segregation between dendritic and interdendritic regions.
The initial alloy has significantly reduced room-temperature fracture strain.
Approximately 4 at.% Cr is to be added to the Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy.
Adding approximately 4 at.% Cr induces a C15 Laves phase with an AB2 structure.
The Cr-induced Laves phase occupies approximately 4 vol.% of the alloy.
The Laves phase has a reticulated, interconnected morphology along grain boundaries and interdendritic regions.
The interconnected Laves-phase network impedes crack extension by creating a tortuous crack path that increases fracture surface area and energy dissipation.
The Laves-phase network also acts as a stress concentrator that initiates microcracks.
Cr solute atoms distort the BCC matrix lattice because of atomic-size mismatch with Hf, Mo, Ta, Ti, and Zr.
Cr-induced lattice distortion raises the Peierls barrier for dislocation motion and thereby produces solid-solution hardening.
Phase-boundary cracking combined with restricted dislocation glide causes premature failure and reduced ductility.
Cr addition increases yield strength through solid-solution hardening.
The Cr-modified alloy will exhibit brittle fracture with intergranular or interdendritic cracking along the Laves-phase network.
The Cr-free baseline alloy has higher fracture strain and contains no Laves phase.
Cr solute causes contraction of the BCC matrix lattice parameter.
Cr has a smaller atomic radius than each of Hf, Mo, Ta, Ti, and Zr.
Laves-phase formation occurs only above approximately 3 at.% Cr.
Laves-phase precipitation requires a sufficiently permissive cooling or annealing condition.
Reticulated Laves-phase morphology requires solidification conditions that promote interdendritic segregation.

contradictions.description: The material_initial_state describes the Cr-free Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy as already having significantly reduced fracture strain, whereas the baseline says the Cr-free alloy has higher fracture strain, and the main hypothesis attributes the low fracture strain to adding Cr.
